Q: Why Rust is taking a ton of my disk space and how to make it use less A:

As long as your Cargo.toml has all the correct dependancies details you just need the cargo.toml file and the actual code in the src folder. It speeds up the compiling having the compiler have easy local access to those build files but you dont need it.

Q: Why does Python asyncio performance decrease when creating too many small tasks? A:

There is no "performance decrease"- there is an overhead time to create and execute the single line of code for each of these tasks.

Scaling from 100_000 to 1_000_000 tasks with your snippet actually show a better than linear time - Since these tasks actually perform no asynchronous wait, just a yielding to the loop - the CPU is expected to be 100% busy running this code - and due to asyncio nature, it does that in a single thread - and therefore, in a single processor core.

Q: Why is my program throwing an illegal instruction error? A:

Your compiler has literally inserted a "generate undefined instruction exception" instruction at the end of your int travelling(int bal) function because although it was declared to return an int, there is no return <some int value>; at all in it. That's "undefined behavior" (UB) and the compiler can do anything it wants, like deleting your computer's hard drive. It was being nice in this case though.

You can see the generated processor instructions for your C++ function in e.g. Godbold (https://godbolt.org/z/9GMKnjsT8), then you see that

  1. It generates the ud2 instruction (generate undefined instruction exception, see (https://mudongliang.github.io/x86/html/file_module_x86_id_318.html)

  2. It gives you a warning telling you what's wrong

Hence you should:

  • change your travelling() function to return void. It's just a print function and doesn't need to return anyhting.

  • check compiler warnings more throughly or compile with -pedantic to make the compiler refuse compilation when a warning occurs. Enable (most) of the warnings with -Wall -Wextra.

Q: How to redirect stderr and stdout to /dev/null? A:

There are two problems here:

ls -a $PWD/*/bin/activate 2>&1 /dev/null

The order of redirection is not the right (you redirect the errors in the std output) and /dev/null is not prefixed with a stream redirection.

You should first redirect the std output into /dev/null and then redirect the std error into the same stream than the std output (that is /dev/null) :

ls -a $PWD/*/bin/activate > /dev/null 2>&1

Q: join_by() where key in x can match two keys in y A:

With sqldf:

sqldf::sqldf(
  "SELECT a.*, b.*
   FROM a 
   LEFT JOIN b 
   ON a.key = b.key1 OR a.key = b.key2"
)

#>   key else1 key1 key2  else2  else3
#> 1   1   cup    1    5 banana  blues
#> 2   2 plate         2 banana   jazz
#> 3   3  bowl         3 banana reggae
#> 4   4   jug         4   pear    ska

Or with powerjoin:

powerjoin::power_left_join(
  a, b, 
  by = ~ dplyr::if_else(.x$key == .y$key1 | 
                          .x$key == .y$key2, 
                        TRUE, FALSE, FALSE)
  )

Or fuzzyjoin:

fuzzyjoin::fuzzy_join(
  a, b,
  multi_by = c("key" = "key1", "key" = "key2"),
  multi_match_fun = \(x, y) {
    x[, 1] == y[, 1] | x[, 2] == y[, 2]
  },
  mode = "left"
)
